title: Put one fix onto the release branch

scenario.brief:
**The ticket.** Customers on the shipped version `release/1.4` are seeing tax amounts with too many decimals. You already fixed this on `main` — the commit *"fix: round tax to whole cents"*. But `main` has also moved on with a new discounts feature that is **not** ready for release.

You can't just merge `main` into `release/1.4` — that would drag the unfinished discounts along. You want **only that one fix**.

**The tool for this is `git cherry-pick`.** It copies a single commit from one branch onto another.

**Your steps.**

1. Switch to the release branch: `git switch release/1.4`.
2. Copy just the fix onto it: `git cherry-pick <the fix commit>`. (Its id is shown in the graph on the right, or use `git log main` to find it.)

That's it. The fix lands on `release/1.4`, and the unfinished discounts stay on `main`.
scenario.whyItMatters: Real products have more than one living version. Cherry-pick is how teams get an urgent fix to customers on an old release without shipping half-finished work that happens to sit next to it on `main`.

hints: Move onto the branch you want the fix to land on.
`git switch release/1.4` moves HEAD there. `git status` confirms the branch name.

objectives.title: Cherry-pick the tax fix — and only the fix
objectives.description: release/1.4's pricing.js should round the tax, and the unfinished discounts must not come along.
hints: Cherry-pick copies one commit by its id onto the current branch — exactly one, not everything on main.
Find the fix with `git log main --oneline` (look for "round tax"), then `git cherry-pick <that id>`.
Type: `git cherry-pick {{label:fix:short}}`. If `src/discount.js` appears on release/1.4, you picked too much.

debrief.summary: You copied a single fix from main onto the live release branch with cherry-pick, leaving unfinished work behind.
internals: `git cherry-pick <id>` took the change that commit introduced (the difference between it and its parent), and re-applied that same change on top of release/1.4 as a brand-new commit with a new id.
It is a copy, not a move: the original fix commit still sits on main, untouched.
Because release/1.4 had the old pricing.js and the fix only touched those lines, it applied cleanly with no conflict.
The discounts commit was never picked, so src/discount.js never reached the release branch.

keyCommands.note: Move onto the branch that should receive the fix.
Copy one commit onto the current branch.

commonMistakes: Merging main into the release branch and dragging unfinished work along.
Forgetting to switch branches first, so the fix lands back on main where it already is.
debrief.atWork: Maintained software usually has a current release and a main branch that is ahead of it. Cherry-pick is the everyday tool for back-porting a fix to the release customers actually run.
debrief.interview: "How do you get one fix onto an old release without the rest of main?" Answer: cherry-pick that single commit onto the release branch.
